notes: Eval target is the plan-reviewer SUBAGENT (the review intelligence, correctness lens plus YAGNI lens). With-skill arm dispatches subagent_type=plan-reviewer; baseline arm dispatches general-purpose with a plain 'review this plan' ask. Each fixture is a self-contained mini-codebase + plan.md with a known planted outcome. Fixtures 0-2 use the older '## Affected files' plan form on purpose (fallback path); yagni-bloat uses the superpowers 7.0 form (Spec header, per-task Files blocks).

evals.name: caller-breakage
evals.prompt: Review the implementation plan at skills/plan-reviewer/fixtures/caller-breakage/plan.md against the code in skills/plan-reviewer/fixtures/caller-breakage/. Surface any problems before I start coding.
evals.expected_output: A Blocker: the plan renames/changes the signature of validate_token but lists only src/auth.py as affected, while src/api.py and src/middleware.py both import and call validate_token -> caller breakage. Output follows the strict schema.

assertions.name: schema_present
assertions.text: Output contains '## Findings', '### Blockers', '### Warnings', '### Suggestions', '### YAGNI' and '## Context inspected' headers.

assertions.name: finding_tag_format
assertions.text: Every severity bullet matches the regex ^- \[(B|W|S)\d+\] and every YAGNI bullet matches ^- \[Y[1-7]\].

assertions.name: no_fabricated_refs
assertions.text: Every file path cited in a finding exists in the fixture (auth.py, api.py, middleware.py); no invented paths.

assertions.name: blocker_present
assertions.text: At least one Blocker [B*] is raised.

assertions.name: caller_breakage_identified
assertions.text: A finding references api.py and/or middleware.py as the broken callers of validate_token.

evals.name: clean-plan
evals.prompt: Review the implementation plan at skills/plan-reviewer/fixtures/clean-plan/plan.md against the code in skills/plan-reviewer/fixtures/clean-plan/. Surface any problems before I start coding.
evals.expected_output: No Blockers, no Warnings, no YAGNI findings. The plan adds a brand-new subtract() with no callers and includes a test. Ideally zero findings (anti-padding); at most a minor Suggestion. Output follows the strict schema.

assertions.name: schema_present
assertions.text: Output contains '## Findings', '### Blockers', '### Warnings', '### Suggestions', '### YAGNI' and '## Context inspected' headers.

assertions.name: finding_tag_format
assertions.text: Every severity bullet matches the regex ^- \[(B|W|S)\d+\] and every YAGNI bullet matches ^- \[Y[1-7]\].

assertions.name: no_blockers_or_warnings
assertions.text: Zero Blockers [B*] and zero Warnings [W*] are raised on this clean plan.

assertions.name: no_yagni_findings
assertions.text: The YAGNI tier is NONE and there are zero [Y*] bullets.

assertions.name: lean_not_padded
assertions.text: At most one finding total (Suggestion) - the reviewer does not pad a clean plan to look thorough.

evals.expected_output: A security finding tagged 'severity-override: security': removing os.path.basename and joining the user-supplied name directly enables path traversal (e.g. ?name=../../etc/passwd). References src/files.py. Output follows the strict schema.

assertions.name: schema_present

assertions.name: finding_tag_format
assertions.text: Every severity bullet matches the regex ^- \[(B|W|S)\d+\] and every YAGNI bullet matches ^- \[Y[1-7]\].

assertions.name: no_fabricated_refs

assertions.name: security_tagged

assertions.name: traversal_location_identified

evals.name: yagni-bloat
evals.prompt: Review the implementation plan at skills/plan-reviewer/fixtures/yagni-bloat/plan.md against the code in skills/plan-reviewer/fixtures/yagni-bloat/. Surface any problems before I start coding.
evals.expected_output: YAGNI tier HARD with Y4 scored against spec.md: [Y4] the profanity filter is outside the spec, [Y1] ISlugifier has one implementation, [Y2] formatStringHelper has a single caller, and slugifyConfig is a knob nothing flips ([Y3], or [Y4] since the spec rules configurability out). The TypeError guard on non-string input is NOT flagged: the route passes req.body.title unchecked, a trust boundary. Output follows the strict schema.

assertions.name: schema_present
assertions.text: Output contains '## Findings', '### Blockers', '### Warnings', '### Suggestions', '### YAGNI' and '## Context inspected' headers, plus the '**YAGNI tier:**' and '**Y4:**' lines.

assertions.name: finding_tag_format
assertions.text: Every severity bullet matches the regex ^- \[(B|W|S)\d+\]; every YAGNI bullet matches ^- \[Y[1-7]\] followed by its canonical label (speculative abstraction, single-caller wrapper, dead config flag, feature outside request, premature optimization, existing utility, defensive code).

assertions.name: tier_hard_y4_scored
assertions.text: The YAGNI tier is HARD and the Y4 line says scored.

assertions.name: profanity_cut
assertions.text: A [Y4] finding names the profanity filter (filterProfanity / profanity-filter.ts).

assertions.name: abstraction_cut
assertions.text: A [Y1] finding names ISlugifier.

assertions.name: wrapper_cut
assertions.text: A [Y2] finding names formatStringHelper.

assertions.name: config_cut
assertions.text: A [Y3] or [Y4] finding names slugifyConfig.

assertions.name: carve_out_respected
assertions.text: No finding of any kind asks to remove the TypeError guard for non-string input; it sits at a trust boundary (req.body.title, src/routes/posts.ts).
